skill.name: commit-prepare
skill.description: Prepare conventional commit messages by reviewing git changes, staging decisions, and commit safety checks.
skill.summary: Helps generate and execute well-structured conventional commits from local git changes.
skill.author: ByronWilliamsCPA

security_audit.summary: The static findings are documentation examples for normal git commit preparation, not unsafe command execution or network behavior. The skill asks for confirmation before committing, warns against bypassing hooks, and includes a secrets check reminder. No prompt injection attempt or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Broad staging can include unintended files if used carelessly.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer staging specific files by default, and reserve git add . for cases where the user has reviewed all changed and untracked files.

remediation.issue: The heredoc commit example can be misused if commit text is copied without review.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the requirement to show the full commit message before execution and avoid interpolating unreviewed shell text into commit commands.

content.value_statement: Writing clear commit messages takes time and requires context from the working tree. This skill reviews git changes, suggests conventional commit messages, and guides safe commit execution.
actual_capabilities: Runs git status and git diff commands to understand staged and unstaged changes.
Classifies changes into conventional commit types such as feat, fix, docs, test, and chore.
Drafts commit subjects, bodies, and footers using conventional commit format.
Asks before staging files or executing a commit.
Recommends splitting unrelated changes into separate commits.
Includes safety reminders for secrets, large binaries, hooks, and pushed commits.
limitations: Requires a local git repository with readable working tree state.
Does not replace human review of staged files or sensitive data.
Cannot know project-specific commit policy unless the user provides it.
May need user confirmation before staging, committing, or pushing changes.

use_cases.title: Create a commit from staged changes
use_cases.description: Review staged diffs and produce a concise conventional commit message before committing.

use_cases.title: Split mixed work into logical commits
use_cases.description: Identify unrelated changes and suggest separate commit messages for each logical unit.

use_cases.title: Teach commit message structure
use_cases.description: Explain which conventional commit type and scope fit a set of changes.

prompt_templates.title: Suggest a commit message
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and suggest a conventional commit message. Do not commit yet.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare and confirm a commit
prompt_templates.scenario: Standard prompt for a ready working tree.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my git status, review the staged diff, draft a commit message, and ask before committing.

prompt_templates.title: Split unrelated changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current changes and tell me if they should be split into separate commits. Suggest messages for each commit.

prompt_templates.title: Audit commit safety before execution
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for release or pull request preparation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare commits for this branch, check for secrets or large binaries, avoid bypassing hooks, and explain any risky staging choices before acting.

output_examples.output: Suggested commit: feat(auth): add OAuth token refresh. The message includes a short body explaining token refresh behavior and test coverage. The assistant asks for confirmation before committing.

output: Shows changed files and unstaged changes.
Warns that staging all files may include unrelated work.
Offers to stage specific files or review the diff first.

output_examples.output: The assistant identifies multiple logical changes, recommends separate commits, and proposes one conventional commit message for each change group.

best_practices: Review staged changes before asking the skill to commit them.
Use specific file staging when the working tree contains unrelated changes.
Provide issue numbers, release notes, or team conventions when they affect the commit message.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to commit secrets, credentials, or generated binaries without review.
Do not use one commit for unrelated bug fixes, features, and documentation changes.
Do not bypass hooks or amend pushed commits unless you understand the shared repository impact.

faq.question: Does this skill create commits automatically?
faq.answer: It is designed to ask for confirmation before executing a commit. Users should review the message and staged files first.

faq.question: Which commit format does it use?
faq.answer: It uses conventional commits with type, optional scope, subject, body, and footer fields.

faq.question: Can it handle breaking changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can mark breaking changes with an exclamation mark and add a breaking change footer.

faq.question: Can it split changes into multiple commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify unrelated changes and suggest separate commit messages for each logical group.

faq.question: Does it check for secrets?
faq.answer: The skill instructs the assistant to check for secrets and credentials before committing, but users should still review sensitive files.

faq.question: Does it push commits to a remote repository?
faq.answer: It may suggest pushing after a successful commit, but pushing should require explicit user approval.
